notes: SR88 Oliver Bonas Home. Same access route as bs88/cl88. Sitemap.xml + main nav expose an extensive /new-in/* taxonomy. The generic '/new-in' and '/new-in/all' ('All New In', live header '906 styles') are SITEWIDE (Department facet: Home 249, Fashion 102, Jewellery 179, Accessories 249, Gift 79, Beauty 43, Furniture 4) with no isolable homeware-only bookmarkable URL (selecting the Home facet did not change the URL) - excluded per this pass's mixed-department rule. Also tried the obvious homeware-scoped URL shapes /homeware/new-in and /homeware/category/new-in: both resolve/canonicalize (rel=canonical) straight back to the generic sitewide /new-in page (same title 'New In | Shop Latest Arrivals Online', same breadcrumb 'New in') - i.e. they are not distinct homeware listings, just alias paths, and were excluded. The genuine homeware-scoped New Arrivals category, structurally parallel to /homeware/category/bestsellers, is https://www.oliverbonas.com/homeware/category/new, titled 'New In Homeware' (H1 'New In Homeware', live-rendered count 'New In Homeware 384 styles'; Filters modal shows only a Product Type facet, no Department facet, confirming the listing is already homeware-pure). This is reported as the primary row. In addition, the site exposes several seasonally-curated /new-in/* 'edit' pages that are homeware-themed by name/breadcrumb rather than mixed sitewide: (1) /new-in/new-season-home, SEO title 'Autumn Home Edit', breadcrumb/Klevu categoryPath 'New In;Autumn Home' - Filters modal Department facet shows Home (94) Furniture (6) Internal Ads (1), so 94 is the Home-only subset; (2) /new-in/edit-2, H1 'Coastal Living' (SEO title 'Coastal Home | Striped Homeware'), live header '82 styles', all-homeware breadcrumb 'Home | Coastal Living'; (3) /new-in/shop-the-edit, H1 'Colourful Home', live header '64 styles'. All three are genuine PLPs (real product grids, Sort/Filter controls, no load-more/pagination gaps found on scroll) and are almost certainly overlapping subsets of the comprehensive 384-item New In Homeware listing above rather than additive population - included as separate rows per the brief's 'category/product overlap is expected, not an error' rule, but each flagged as an ambiguous 'New Collection'-style page per the brief's explicit test, since none of the three page names/copy state outright that the products are the newest additions (they read as style/theme edits that happen to live under the /new-in/ URL path) versus /homeware/category/new which unambiguously identifies itself as 'New In Homeware'. Checked but NOT individually opened for validation, for time/scope reasons, given none of their SSR <title> tags mention Home/homeware and the site's own Department facet on /new-in/all shows Home is a minority slice of each of these general campaign buckets: /new-in/as-seen-in-press ('As Seen In Press'), /new-in/as-seen-on-socials ('As Seen On Socials'), /new-in/back-in-stock ('Back In Stock Products'), /new-in/campaign ('Summer Style Edit'), /new-in/campaign-2 ('Pink & Burgundy Edit'), /new-in/founder-favourites ('Founder Favourites'), /new-in/must-haves ('Must-haves'), /new-in/new-season ('New In Fashion' - explicitly fashion, not home), /new-in/trending-now ('Trending Now'). Also cross-checked /new-in/best-sellers ('Most Wanted | Bestsellers') which is the Bestsellers-brief's concern, not New Arrivals. Site search (/search) is robots.txt-disallowed so was not used; relied on nav, footer, and sitemap.xml enumeration instead.
